Please inspect the relevant code and nearby endian swapping methods, and identify an appropriate minimal C++ patch.

The sanitizer reports a global-buffer-overflow at arrow/cpp/src/arrow/array/util.cc lines 210-212. The MonthDayNano visitor allocates an output buffer equal to data_->buffers[1]->size() but loops over data_->length, which comes from malformed IPC metadata and may exceed the number of complete MonthDayNanos structs in the values buffer. Nearby ByteSwapBuffer and Decimal128/256 paths derive the iteration count from the actual buffer size. I attempted the minimal production patch to cache buffer_size and use buffer_size / sizeof(MonthDayNanos) as the loop bound, but the apply_patch tool unexpectedly classified util.cc as a fuzzer harness and rejected the edit, even though the actual harness is arrow/cpp/src/arrow/ipc/stream_fuzz.cc. I need confirmation of the source role and potentially another root-cause patch strategy in an editable production C++ file.
